# caplinks

Capability links: hand someone a link to one thing, with no account. The token is the permission; a password may gate it; it expires; it can be revoked; password attempts are limited. Standard library only, no web framework.

```default
pip install caplinks
```

```python
from caplinks import CapabilityLinks

links = CapabilityLinks()  # records in a dict; pass any MutableMapping to persist them
rec = links.create({"doc": "report-1"}, password="open sesame", expires="7d")
url = f"https://example.com/s/{rec['token']}/"

state, stored = links.status(rec["token"])   # "ok", "expired" or "missing"
links.check_password(stored, "open sesame")  # True
cookie = links.unlock_value(stored)          # what a correct password earns
links.unlocked(stored, cookie, max_age_s=3600)  # True, until the password changes or the link is revoked
links.revoke(rec["token"])                   # now "missing"
```

## What is in it

- `CapabilityLinks`: create, read, list and revoke links, and gate them on a password. Records are plain dicts in any `MutableMapping` keyed by token: the generic fields are `token`, `created`, `expires`, `password` (a hash) and `revoked`; your own fields (what the link reaches) sit beside them.
- Gating an id you already have: `create(..., token=existing_id)` keeps the id; `set_password(token, pw_or_None)` and `set_expires(token, when)` change a live link later (a new password ends every open unlock).
- `ScryptHasher` (stdlib scrypt) behind the `PasswordHasher` protocol (`hash`, `verify -> bool`): pass `hasher=` for argon2 or anything else.
- `parse_expires` reads what people write (`30m`, `12h`, `7d`, `2w`, `2026-11-01` meaning the end of that day UTC, an ISO timestamp, `never`) and refuses the past; `is_expired` fails closed.
- `SlidingWindowLimiter` behind the `RateLimiter` protocol (`allow(key) -> bool`): count password attempts per client, per link, or both. It is per process; a shared limiter of the same shape (Redis, say) fits where several workers serve the links.

The unlock value is an HMAC keyed by the stored password hash, so changing the password or revoking the link (which clears the hash) ends every open session at once.

## What stays with your app

What a link reaches (its scope), how it is served (routes, cookie name, headers), and the attempt policy. `annals` (share links) is the first host.

## Seams

| keyword            | default          | for                                                 |
|--------------------|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `store`            | `dict`           | persistence: a dol store, a file-backed mapping, S3 |
| `hasher`           | `ScryptHasher()` | argon2id or another scheme                          |
| `clock`            | `now_utc`        | tests that pin the time                             |
| `min_password_len` | 8                | a stricter or laxer gate                            |

A store that cannot vouch for a record raises `KeyError`, `ValueError` or `OSError` when it is read, and the link is then missing; so is a record whose generic fields have the wrong types. Every failure closes the link.

# _autosummary/caplinks.expiry.html.md

# caplinks.expiry

When a link stops working: reading an expiry the way a person writes one.

An expiry is stored as an ISO UTC timestamp (or `None` for never). [`parse_expires()`](_autosummary/caplinks.expiry.html.md#caplinks.expiry.parse_expires)
reads what a person types (`7d`, `2026-11-01`, an ISO timestamp, `never`);
[`is_expired()`](_autosummary/caplinks.expiry.html.md#caplinks.expiry.is_expired) checks a record against the clock and fails closed on a value it
cannot read.

### Module Attributes

| [`DURATION_UNITS`](_autosummary/caplinks.expiry.html.md#caplinks.expiry.DURATION_UNITS)   | duration suffixes accepted by [`parse_expires()`](_autosummary/caplinks.expiry.html.md#caplinks.expiry.parse_expires) (`30m`, `12h`, `7d`, `2w`)   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`NEVER`](_autosummary/caplinks.expiry.html.md#caplinks.expiry.NEVER)            | words that mean "no expiry"                                                                                                 |

|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`is_expired`](_autosummary/caplinks.expiry.html.md#caplinks.expiry.is_expired)(record, \*[, now])   | True when the record has an expiry and it is reached (a bad one counts as reached). |
| [`now_utc`](_autosummary/caplinks.expiry.html.md#caplinks.expiry.now_utc)()                       | The current time, UTC, second precision (the clock every default reads).            |

Raises `ValueError` on a value that is not a timestamp.

  [`datetime`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### caplinks.expiry.is_expired(record, , now=None)

True when the record has an expiry and it is reached (a bad one counts as reached).

```pycon
>>> is_expired({"expires": None}), is_expired({"expires": "garbage"})
(False, True)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### caplinks.expiry.now_utc()

The current time, UTC, second precision (the clock every default reads).

* **Return type:**
  [`datetime`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime)

### caplinks.expiry.parse_expires(value, , now=None)

An expiry as an ISO UTC timestamp, or `None` for never.

`None`, `""` and `"never"` mean never. Accepts a duration (`30m`, `12h`,
`7d`, `2w`), a date (`2026-11-01`: the END of that day, UTC, so the link works
through the day named), an ISO timestamp (a naive one is UTC), or a `datetime`.
A moment already past is refused.

```pycon
>>> t0 = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
>>> parse_expires("2d", now=t0)
'2026-01-03T00:00:00+00:00'
>>> parse_expires("2026-01-05", now=t0)
'2026-01-05T23:59:59+00:00'
>>> parse_expires("never") is None
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/caplinks.html.md

# caplinks

Capability links: an unguessable token, an optional password gate, expiry, attempt limits.

The parts every app needs to hand someone a link to one thing, with no account: the
token is the permission, a password may gate it, it expires, it can be revoked, and
password attempts are limited. Standard library only; no web framework. What a link
reaches (its scope) and how it is served stay with the app.

```pycon
>>> links = CapabilityLinks()  # records in a dict; pass any MutableMapping to persist
>>> rec = links.create({"doc": "report-1"}, password="open sesame", expires="7d")
>>> state, stored = links.status(rec["token"])
>>> state, links.check_password(stored, "open sesame")
('ok', True)
>>> cookie = links.unlock_value(stored)
>>> links.unlocked(stored, cookie, max_age_s=3600)
True
```

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Create, read, list and revoke capability links, and gate them on a password.

`store` maps token to record (a `dict` by default, in process); `hasher`
hashes link passwords (stdlib scrypt by default); `clock` returns the current UTC
`datetime` (tests pin it); `min_password_len` is the shortest password accepted.

#### check_password(record, password)

Whether `password` opens `record` (constant time inside the hasher).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### create(fields=None, , password=None, expires='7d', token=None)

Make a link carrying the host’s `fields`; return its record without the hash.

`expires` is anything [`caplinks.expiry.parse_expires()`](_autosummary/caplinks.expiry.html.md#caplinks.expiry.parse_expires) reads, 7 days by
default (`"never"` for none); `password` gates the link. `token` gates an
id that already exists (a host whose links must not change): it must look like
a token ([`check_token()`](_autosummary/caplinks.html.md#caplinks.check_token)) and be unused; leave it out for a fresh one. The
caller then owns the id’s randomness: use 128 random bits, as [`new_token()`](_autosummary/caplinks.html.md#caplinks.new_token).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### list(, include_inactive=False)

Every live link, newest first, without hashes; `include_inactive` adds
revoked and expired ones.

Each record gains `active` (neither revoked nor expired).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](_autosummary/caplinks.html.md#caplinks.CapabilityLinks.list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### record(token)

A copy of the stored record (hash included), revoked or not; `None` if none.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### revoke(token)

End a link now (idempotent). The record stays, as a tombstone.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### set_expires(token, expires)

Move an unrevoked link’s expiry (anything [`parse_expires()`](_autosummary/caplinks.html.md#caplinks.parse_expires) reads;
`"never"` for none). An expired link may be given a later one; a revoked link
stays revoked (`KeyError`).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### set_password(token, password)

Give an unrevoked link a new password, or `None` to open it.

A new password ends every open unlock at once. A revoked link stays revoked
(`KeyError`).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### status(token)

`("ok" | "expired" | "missing", record)`; a revoked link is `missing`.

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]

#### unlock_max_age(record, , max_age_s)

How long an unlock should last, in seconds: `max_age_s`, never past expiry.

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

#### unlock_value(record)

What a correct password earns, to send back on later requests: `<epoch>.<mac>`.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### unlocked(record, value, , max_age_s)

Whether `value` is a live unlock of `record` (no password: always).

A revoked record is never unlocked, whatever the caller checked before.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### *class* caplinks.RateLimiter(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Decide whether one more attempt keyed by `key` is allowed now.

### *class* caplinks.ScryptHasher(n=16384, r=8, p=1, salt_bytes=16, dklen=32)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Stdlib `hashlib.scrypt`, stored as `scrypt$n$r$p$salt$hash` (base64).

The parameters travel with the hash, so raising `n` later still verifies old
hashes. `n=2**14, r=8` costs ~16 MB and tens of ms per check, which a host’s
attempt limit ([`caplinks.limits`](_autosummary/caplinks.limits.html.md#module-caplinks.limits)) bounds.

### *class* caplinks.SlidingWindowLimiter(\*, max_per_window=10, window_s=300.0, max_keys=50000, clock=<built-in function monotonic>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

At most `max_per_window` hits per key per window; in memory, per process.

Each worker counts alone (two workers allow twice the attempts); pass a shared
limiter when that matters. The least recently seen keys are dropped past
`max_keys`.

```pycon
>>> t = [0.0]
>>> lim = SlidingWindowLimiter(max_per_window=2, window_s=10, clock=lambda: t[0])
>>> [lim.allow("a"), lim.allow("a"), lim.allow("a"), lim.allow("b")]
[True, True, False, True]
>>> t[0] = 10.0; lim.allow("a")
True
```

# _autosummary/caplinks.limits.html.md

# caplinks.limits

Limiting password attempts: the `allow(key) -> bool` protocol and an in-memory default.

A host decides what to count (one client on one link, every wrong password a link
takes, …) and keys the limiter accordingly. The protocol is the shape of
`heed.security`’s limiters, so its `RedisRateLimiter` (one count shared by every
worker) fits wherever a [`RateLimiter`](_autosummary/caplinks.limits.html.md#caplinks.limits.RateLimiter) is asked for.

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_MAX_PER_WINDOW`](_autosummary/caplinks.limits.html.md#caplinks.limits.DFLT_MAX_PER_WINDOW)   | attempts one key may make in each window, by default                |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_MAX_KEYS`](_autosummary/caplinks.limits.html.md#caplinks.limits.DFLT_MAX_KEYS)         | keys tracked at most, so a flood of addresses cannot exhaust memory |

### Classes

| [`RateLimiter`](_autosummary/caplinks.limits.html.md#caplinks.limits.RateLimiter)(\*args, \*\*kwargs)                 | Decide whether one more attempt keyed by `key` is allowed now.            |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SlidingWindowLimiter`](_autosummary/caplinks.limits.html.md#caplinks.limits.SlidingWindowLimiter)(\*[, max_per_window, ...]) | At most `max_per_window` hits per key per window; in memory, per process. |

# _autosummary/caplinks.links.html.md

# caplinks.links

Capability links: a record behind an unguessable token, with an optional password gate.

Knowing the token is the permission. A record is a plain dict, stored in any
`MutableMapping` keyed by token; the generic fields are [`RECORD_FIELDS`](_autosummary/caplinks.links.html.md#caplinks.links.RECORD_FIELDS), and a
host puts what the link reaches (its scope) in fields of its own beside them:

```default
{"token": "<22 url-safe chars, 128 random bits>",
 "created": "<iso>", "expires": "<iso>" | None,
 "password": "scrypt$..." | None,     # a hash; the password is never stored
 "revoked": "<iso>" | None,           # a tombstone: a revoked link is missing
 ...the host's fields...}
```

A correct password earns an unlock value (a cookie, for a web host): an HMAC keyed by
the stored hash, so a new password, or a revoke, which clears the hash, ends every open
session at once.

The store contract: a store that cannot vouch for a record (unreadable, damaged, or
missing the host’s own fields) raises `KeyError`, `ValueError` or `OSError` when
it is read, and the link is then missing. A record whose generic fields have the wrong
types is missing too: every failure closes the link.

```pycon
>>> links = CapabilityLinks()
>>> rec = links.create({"what": "report-1"}, password="open sesame", expires="7d")
>>> links.status(rec["token"])[0], rec["protected"], "password" in rec
('ok', True, False)
```

### Module Attributes

| [`RECORD_FIELDS`](_autosummary/caplinks.links.html.md#caplinks.links.RECORD_FIELDS)    | the fields every record has; a host's own fields may not reuse these names             |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_EXPIRES`](_autosummary/caplinks.links.html.md#caplinks.links.DFLT_EXPIRES)     | a link lasts this long unless told otherwise (`"never"` for no expiry)                 |
| [`MIN_PASSWORD_LEN`](_autosummary/caplinks.links.html.md#caplinks.links.MIN_PASSWORD_LEN) | the shortest link password accepted (a gate tried from anywhere must not be guessable) |

### Functions

| [`check_token`](_autosummary/caplinks.links.html.md#caplinks.links.check_token)(token)    | Return `token`; raise `ValueError` on anything that could not be one.    |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`new_token`](_autosummary/caplinks.links.html.md#caplinks.links.new_token)()           | A fresh link token: 128 random bits, url-safe.                           |
| [`public_record`](_autosummary/caplinks.links.html.md#caplinks.links.public_record)(record) | A record without its password hash; `protected` says whether it has one. |

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### create(fields=None, , password=None, expires='7d', token=None)

Make a link carrying the host’s `fields`; return its record without the hash.

`expires` is anything [`caplinks.expiry.parse_expires()`](_autosummary/caplinks.expiry.html.md#caplinks.expiry.parse_expires) reads, 7 days by
default (`"never"` for none); `password` gates the link. `token` gates an
id that already exists (a host whose links must not change): it must look like
a token ([`check_token()`](_autosummary/caplinks.links.html.md#caplinks.links.check_token)) and be unused; leave it out for a fresh one. The
caller then owns the id’s randomness: use 128 random bits, as [`new_token()`](_autosummary/caplinks.links.html.md#caplinks.links.new_token).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### list(, include_inactive=False)

Every live link, newest first, without hashes; `include_inactive` adds
revoked and expired ones.

Each record gains `active` (neither revoked nor expired).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](_autosummary/caplinks.links.html.md#caplinks.links.CapabilityLinks.list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### record(token)

A copy of the stored record (hash included), revoked or not; `None` if none.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### revoke(token)

End a link now (idempotent). The record stays, as a tombstone.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### set_expires(token, expires)

Move an unrevoked link’s expiry (anything `parse_expires()` reads;
`"never"` for none). An expired link may be given a later one; a revoked link
stays revoked (`KeyError`).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### set_password(token, password)

Give an unrevoked link a new password, or `None` to open it.

A new password ends every open unlock at once. A revoked link stays revoked
(`KeyError`).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### status(token)

`("ok" | "expired" | "missing", record)`; a revoked link is `missing`.

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]

#### unlock_max_age(record, , max_age_s)

How long an unlock should last, in seconds: `max_age_s`, never past expiry.

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

#### unlock_value(record)

What a correct password earns, to send back on later requests: `<epoch>.<mac>`.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### unlocked(record, value, , max_age_s)

Whether `value` is a live unlock of `record` (no password: always).

A revoked record is never unlocked, whatever the caller checked before.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### caplinks.links.DFLT_EXPIRES *= '7d'*

a link lasts this long unless told otherwise (`"never"` for no expiry)

### caplinks.links.MIN_PASSWORD_LEN *= 8*

the shortest link password accepted (a gate tried from anywhere must not be guessable)

### caplinks.links.RECORD_FIELDS *= ('token', 'created', 'expires', 'password', 'revoked')*

the fields every record has; a host’s own fields may not reuse these names

### caplinks.links.check_token(token)

Return `token`; raise `ValueError` on anything that could not be one.

```pycon
>>> check_token("../../etc/passwd")
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
ValueError: not a link token
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### caplinks.links.new_token()

A fresh link token: 128 random bits, url-safe.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### caplinks.links.public_record(record)

A record without its password hash; `protected` says whether it has one.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/caplinks.passwords.html.md

# caplinks.passwords

Password hashing for a link’s password gate: a protocol and a stdlib default.

A link password is a gate, not an account: it is hashed once when the link is made and
checked on each unlock. [`ScryptHasher`](_autosummary/caplinks.passwords.html.md#caplinks.passwords.ScryptHasher) needs nothing beyond the standard library;
anything with the same two methods (an argon2id adapter, say) fits the `hasher` seam
of [`caplinks.CapabilityLinks`](_autosummary/caplinks.html.md#caplinks.CapabilityLinks).

```pycon
>>> h = ScryptHasher(n=2**4)  # tiny cost, for the example only
>>> stored = h.hash("correct horse")
>>> stored.startswith("scrypt$"), h.verify(stored, "correct horse"), h.verify(stored, "x")
(True, True, False)
```

### Classes

| [`PasswordHasher`](_autosummary/caplinks.passwords.html.md#caplinks.passwords.PasswordHasher)(\*args, \*\*kwargs)         | What a link needs to gate on a password: `verify` returns a bool, never raises.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ScryptHasher`](_autosummary/caplinks.passwords.html.md#caplinks.passwords.ScryptHasher)([n, r, p, salt_bytes, dklen]) | Stdlib `hashlib.scrypt`, stored as `scrypt$n$r$p$salt$hash` (base64).             |

### *class* caplinks.passwords.PasswordHasher(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

What a link needs to gate on a password: `verify` returns a bool, never raises.

### *class* caplinks.passwords.ScryptHasher(n=16384, r=8, p=1, salt_bytes=16, dklen=32)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Stdlib `hashlib.scrypt`, stored as `scrypt$n$r$p$salt$hash` (base64).

The parameters travel with the hash, so raising `n` later still verifies old
hashes. `n=2**14, r=8` costs ~16 MB and tens of ms per check, which a host’s
attempt limit ([`caplinks.limits`](_autosummary/caplinks.limits.html.md#module-caplinks.limits)) bounds.
